goals: PRIMARY (as posed): estimate nitrate arrival concentration at drinking-water wells from fertilized fields
VALIDATION (as posed): compare simulated well nitrate to external well nitrate records
FALLBACK (feasible proxy): characterize vadose-zone recharge flux and wetting-front travel time as a transport-timing precursor
key_processes: surface nitrogen source from fertilizer application
reactive/solute transport of nitrate through vadose zone and aquifer
lateral groundwater flow from field source to well receptor
vadose-zone unsaturated flow / recharge transmission (the only representable piece)

model_choice.rationale: Subsurface transport to wells is nominally a PFLOTRAN problem, but this stack's PFLOTRAN is FLOW-ONLY and 1-D with no lateral flow, so it cannot represent the source-to-well transport or the concentration the question demands.
model_choice.coupling_note: ELM->PFLOTRAN one-way coupling could supply a realistic recharge BC for the FALLBACK travel-time proxy, but does not enable nitrate transport; the reactive-transport engine and a lateral-flow model are the true missing pieces.

answerable: vadose-zone recharge flux magnitude per SSURGO soil (ELM or prescribed)
1-D wetting-front / recharge travel time through the unsaturated zone (hydraulic timing proxy only, NOT solute)

not_answerable.why: PFLOTRAN deck is FLOW-ONLY; no solute/reactive transport chemistry is configured — concentration cannot be produced
columns are independent 1-D points; no lateral flow, no stream-aquifer exchange, no well/pumping sink
not_answerable.needs: lateral / regional groundwater flow with well receptors

not_answerable.why: neither ELM (soil/forcing/location levers) nor the PFLOTRAN deck ingests a fertilizer application/nitrogen loading input
no simulated nitrate concentration exists to compare against the observations
not_answerable.needs: reactive transport (above) before any validation is possible

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (fallback proxy only — NOT a nitrate design)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: If the feasible fallback (recharge travel-time characterization) is pursued, ~3 dominant SSURGO texture classes x ~3 replicate columns spans the vadose-zone heterogeneity controlling transmission timing. This does NOT answer the nitrate question and is offered only as a precursor. Elevation is not a stratum: 160 m relief with no fertilizer/transport mechanism gives it no explanatory role here.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in agricultural lowlands with shallow water tables and tile-drainage-prone fine soils, where recharge transmission is fastest and most relevant to any future transport study; flag any column whose real WTD exceeds the 50 m domain cap.
sampling_strategy.replication: ~3 per texture class to expose SSURGO within-class variability; expect solver attrition on extreme soil-contrast columns.

sampling_plan.reason: Fast recharge transmission end-member — shortest wetting-front travel time (hydraulic proxy only, not nitrate).
Intermediate transmission timing spanning the bulk of the basin's cropped soils (proxy only).
Slow-matrix end-member; most relevant to future transport work but attenuates recharge signal strongly (proxy only).

validation_design.comparison: NONE POSSIBLE — no simulated nitrate concentration can be produced by the flow-only stack; validation is blocked until reactive transport exists
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — moot until concentration can be simulated

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: prescribed/ELM-derived recharge BC, native SSURGO soil — FALLBACK travel-time proxy only, NOT a nitrate simulation

requires_capabilities.why: the question asks for arrival CONCENTRATION; current deck is flow-only
requires_capabilities.blocks: all concentration output and all nitrate validation

requires_capabilities.capability: lateral / regional groundwater flow with well receptors and stream-aquifer exchange
requires_capabilities.why: 'from fields to wells' is inherently a lateral source-to-receptor problem; columns are independent 1-D points
requires_capabilities.blocks: any field-to-well pathway and arrival at a well location

requires_capabilities.why: fertilizer loading is the source; no lever in ELM or PFLOTRAN accepts it
requires_capabilities.blocks: representing the nitrate source at all

requires_capabilities.why: arrival is evaluated at specific well points
requires_capabilities.blocks: placing receptors and matching observation records

requires_capabilities.why: supplies a realistic recharge BC for the travel-time proxy
requires_capabilities.blocks: realistic recharge forcing of the proxy study (not the nitrate question)

assumptions: External well nitrate records are point observations of concentration, which the stack cannot currently reproduce.
The fallback recharge/travel-time proxy is offered as a precursor deliverable only; it does NOT answer the user's nitrate question.
Some agricultural lowland columns may have real water tables within the 50 m cap; deep-WTD columns would pin at the bottom boundary and be flagged.
Any recharge/water-table target in the fallback requires spin-up years or a Fan(2013) WTD warm start.
open_questions: Is the goal true nitrate concentration, or would a hydraulic vulnerability/travel-time ranking (feasible fallback) satisfy the decision need?
Can a reactive-transport-enabled PFLOTRAN deck and a fertilizer loading dataset be provisioned? Without both, the question cannot be answered.
Are well locations, screen depths, and a lateral-flow model available, since arrival at a well is a lateral, not 1-D, quantity?
